NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Tuesday said no order was required on a petition challenging the directive to vacate the Central Secretariat Club after the Centre informed the court that it had no plans to allot the premises to anyone at present.The central government made the submission during an earlier hearing of a petition seeking an interim stay on its decision to de-recognise the club, formerly known as Talkatora Club.Taking note of the submission, the court ruled no order was required to be passed."Considering the above, no order is required to be passed. The petitioners are permitted to take away their belongings in the next one week. List on the date already fixed, that is, December 21, 2026," PTI quoted Justice Amit Mahajan as saying.The high court was hearing an application filed by the Central Secretariat Club seeking an ad interim stay on the July 14 de-recognition order and the July 17 eviction order.During the hearing on November 5, the Centre’s counsel submitted that there was no proposal to allot the premises to any party at this stage.The court had earlier issued notice to the central government and sought its response to the petition.The bench of Justice Mahajan was hearing the club’s challenge to the government’s de-recognition order and the eviction notice issued by the estate officer, directing it to vacate its premises in the President’s Estate.In its petition, the club alleged that the Department of Personnel and Training, through its July 14 order, had "arbitrarily, illegally and unconstitutionally" withdrawn the recognition granted to it.The petitioner contended that instead of acting on its complaints about alleged irregularities during the tenure of the ad hoc committee managing its affairs, the authorities withdrew its recognition in February without issuing a show-cause notice.Following the high court’s intervention, the club was granted a hearing, after which a fresh de-recognition order was issued on July 14.The petition described the July 14 de-recognition order and the July 17 eviction order as "ex facie arbitrary, malicious, unconstitutional, and a brazen, colourable exercise of administrative power."It further alleged that the authorities were attempting to use their own "administrative failures" and the "misconduct" of the ad hoc committee to forcibly dispossess the club and shut down the institution, calling it a "violation" of Article 14 of the Constitution and the principles of natural justice.The plea also challenged the eviction order for treating the 107-year-old institution, which had been granted permanent occupancy, as an "unauthorised occupant" on the basis of what it termed an "illegal cancellation" of allotment.
Article Summary: The Delhi high court said no order was required on a petition challenging the directive to vacate the Central Secretariat Club. The Centre informed the court that it had no plans to allot the premises to anyone at present. The central government made the submission during an earlier hearing of a petition seeking an interim stay on its decision to de- recognize the club.

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Tuesday targeted the BJP-led government at the Centre over rising air pollution in Delhi, asking why the national capital was becoming a “Vishwaguru” in pollution.In a post on X, Kharge said that clean air is a fundamental right, not a privilege to be granted by the Government.“Why are we becoming a ‘Vishwaguru’ in air pollution? Piecemeal measures, PR stunts, broken promises and blame games have become the hallmark of the BJP,” he said.Delhi has been witnessing deteriorating air quality following Diwali, with pollution from multiple sources, including stubble burning in neighbouring states, adding to the crisis.The Congress chief alleged that discrepancies in air quality monitoring had raised further questions over the government's handling of pollution.Referring to last year's allegations of water tankers spraying water around air quality monitoring stations to bring down recorded pollution levels, Kharge claimed that this year PM2.5 readings had disappeared from 36 of Delhi's 59 monitoring stations as pollution peaked.He accused the Modi government of failing to address the problem despite identifying air pollution as a major challenge in 2019.The Congress president also cited estimates of deaths linked to air pollution to underline the scale of the public health crisis.According to figures cited in his post, an estimated 17,188 deaths in Delhi in 2023 were attributable to particulate air pollution, accounting for nearly 15% of all deaths, based on Global Burden of Disease and Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air estimates.He also referred to the State of Global Air 2024 report, which estimated that 1,69,400 children under the age of five died from air-pollution-related causes across India in 2021.Kharge further questioned the utilisation of funds earmarked for tackling pollution in Delhi.Citing a September 2026 RTI response, he said Rs 1,154 crore, nearly 60% of Delhi's environmental compensation collections, remained unspent. He also claimed that the city had utilised only 17% of the National Clean Air Programme funds released up to December 2025.Kharge also pointed to the Supreme Court's direction to BJP-ruled Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan to submit detailed responses and proposed measures to tackle the pollution crisis within two weeks.He said the same pattern of toxic air, assurances and blame-shifting returned every year, particularly between October and February.“Year after year, particularly from October to February, the same toxic haze returns, accompanied by the same assurances and the same finger-pointing. Spend the funds. Cut emissions. Enforce the rules,” he said.Kharge ended his post by challenging the Prime Minister to account for the government's efforts to improve air quality.“Will Modi ji dare to give the nation 'Hawa Ka Hisaab'?” he asked.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge asks why Delhi is becoming a ‘Vishwaguru’ in pollution. He accuses the Modi government of failing to address the problem despite identifying air pollution as a major challenge in 2019. The Congress president also cited estimates of deaths linked to air pollution to underline the scale of the public health crisis.

Article Title: SC: Govt has wide powers to compulsorily retire staffer, improve efficiency
Article Text:
Retirement must be based on bona fide assessment, says SC

Retirement must be based on bona fide assessment, says SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has ruled govt has wide powers to compulsorily retire an employee to improve efficiency of administration and that the person aggrieved cannot challenge such a decision on the ground that other similarly placed employees have not met the same fate.Upholding Chhattisgarh govt's decision to compulsorily retire five employees, a bench of Justices Manmohan and Shree Chandrashekhar said the principle of "every person must be heard before being punished", as enshrined in Article 311(2) of Constitution, is not applicable to cases of compulsory retirement because it is neither punitive nor casts aspersion upon an employee's conduct.Justice Manmohan said, "The decision is founded upon the subjective satisfaction of competent authority that the employee's continued retention in service is no longer conducive to public interest."Writing the judgement, Justice Manmohan said, “The ultimate assessment as to whether an officer has become ‘dead wood’ or whether his continuance would be detrimental to administrative efficiency falls within the domain of the executive.”Chhattisgarh additional advocate general Rajat Nair said decisions to compulsorily retire the five ‘assistant’ grade officers was arrived at in public interest for maintaining efficiency of administration after a two-tier scrutiny of their performance, efficiency, track records, integrity and annual confidential records.When such decisions are challenged by aggrieved employees, courts need to re-appreciate or re-evaluate material considered by authorities. “The court is concerned only with whether relevant material existed, whether such material was taken into consideration by competent authority, and whether the conclusion drawn therefrom is one which a reasonable person could have arrived at,” it said while rejecting the appeals.It said, “The power to compulsorily retire a govt servant under applicable service rules is of wide amplitude and is conditional principally by the requirement that the authority must form its opinion bona fide and upon relevant material. Mere fact that another officer, who may appear similarly placed, was not compulsorily retired cannot constitute a valid defence to an otherwise lawful order of compulsory retirement. ”
Article Summary: Supreme Court upholds Chhattisgarh govt's decision to compulsorily retire five employees. Justices Manmohan and Shree Chandrashekhar said the principle of "every person must be heard before being punished" is not applicable to cases of compulsory retirement.

Article Title: 'Scrap Rs 500 notes': CM Naidu seeks to phase out big currency to curb corruption
Article Text:

Naidu claims NDA cut money power in local polls

NEW DELHI: Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Monday renewed his call for withdrawing Rs 500 currency notes, arguing that limiting cash transactions to smaller denominations and encouraging digital payments could help curb corruption.Naidu said he had previously raised the proposal in a report on digital currency submitted to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and intended to continue pressing for the change.“I will keep speaking on this. The notes of Rs 500, Rs 1,000 and Rs. 2,000 should be scrapped. Only notes of Rs 100 and Rs 200 should be retained,” he was quoted as saying by news agency IANS.Speaking at a press conference, the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) chief argued that reducing the circulation of high-value currency would make it harder to use large amounts of cash for corrupt activities. He also stressed the importance of technology in improving economic opportunities.“If technology is perfect, wealth creation and poverty alleviation are not difficult,” he said.Turning to the recent local body elections in Andhra Pradesh, Naidu said the results showed growing public support for the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA). He also claimed that the alliance had managed to reduce the influence of money power in the polls.According to figures shared by the chief minister, the NDA secured 58.9 per cent of the combined vote in urban local body and Parishad elections. This was 3.6 percentage points higher than the 55.3 per cent it received in the 2024 general elections.The YSR Congress Party's (YSRCP) vote share, meanwhile, fell from 39.81 per cent in 2024 to 33.56 per cent in the local body polls, a decline of 6.25 percentage points. The gap between the two sides stood at 25.34 percentage points, Naidu said.He said the alliance's vote share in urban local body elections was 59.9 per cent, compared with 34.3 per cent for the YSRCP. The NDA also recorded a strike rate of 94 per cent in urban areas.In Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections, the alliance polled 57.6 per cent of the votes against the YSRCP's 39.7 per cent. The difference between their vote shares was 17.9 percentage points in rural areas.Naidu said the alliance won 575 of the 659 ZPTC seats across Andhra Pradesh, leading in 27 of the state's 28 districts. The YSRCP managed to win more seats than the alliance only in Alluri Sitarama Raju district. It failed to secure even one ZPTC seat in seven districts.In Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) elections, the NDA won 7,803 of the 9,818 seats. The alliance is also expected to capture around 90 per cent of the Mandal President posts across the state.The chief minister said the alliance's performance was equally strong in urban local bodies. Of the 100 Mayor and Chairperson posts, it won 94, including 12 of the 13 mayoral positions and 82 of the 87 chairperson posts.The TDP secured 70 of these posts, while the Jana Sena Party won 20 and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) four.The alliance also won 3,233 of the 3,941 municipal wards, accounting for 82 per cent of the total. It secured a majority in 95 of the 100 urban local bodies and won every ward in 16 of them.The YSRCP, by comparison, won only four urban local bodies and 558 wards. It failed to win a single ward in 22 urban local bodies, Naidu said.He described the results as a reflection of public backing for good governance, social justice, new leadership and democratic values, adding that the alliance's support had increased significantly since the 2024 general elections.
Article Summary: Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu renewed his call for withdrawing Rs 500 currency notes. He argued that limiting cash transactions to smaller denominations and encouraging digital payments could help curb corruption. “If technology is perfect, wealth creation and poverty alleviation are not difficult,” CM Nadu said.

BENGALURU/NEW DELHI/T'PURAM: Following in Congress-governed Karnataka's footsteps, the Congress-led govt of Keralam Monday started collecting petrol samples to test whether their ethanol content was more than the prescribed 20%, setting up a likely Centre-state confrontation over E20 fuel.Keralam civil supplies minister Anoop Jacob said officials collected six samples each from nine petrol pumps across Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode and Kannur, in the presence of OMC representatives.PESO-approved bottles and trained officials were used, he said, adding that further rounds of testing would follow and prosecution would be initiated if excess blending was detected.This prompted Union minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi to say that states were free to conduct tests but they should avoid political mudslinging. "Let them conduct the tests, whether it is Karnataka or Keralam govt. We have scientific support for it," he said. The minister warned that those creating controversies for political purposes would have to face consequences. Gopi said Centre had permitted 20% blending after assessing scientific feasibility and was implementing the transition gradually.On Monday, Karnataka defended its third-party laboratory findings about ethanol levels of up to 31.2%, rejecting a joint rebuttal by three oil marketing companies - IOCL, BPCL and HPCL.State food and civil supplies minister Rizwan Arshad termed objections raised by the three OMCs "illogical" and accused them of trying to push for a fresh joint survey after recalibrating the ethanol mix.He said state govt would send its findings to Centre, seek changes in testing protocols and demand discounted prices for E20 petrol, stressing that higher ethanol content reduced mileage and raised the effective cost for consumers.Arshad said alleged blending of up to 30% was happening at six terminals where ethanol was mixed with petrol before distribution, not at retail outlets. Karnataka said authorised officials followed prescribed sampling procedures, with labels jointly signed by officials and dealers. After OMC laboratories failed to provide ethanol percentages for the initial 63 samples, the state sent them to NABL-accredited, ISO-certified third-party laboratories.The three OMCs had challenged Karnataka's Oct tests, questioning its sampling and laboratory methodology. They said it did not follow statutory procedures under Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel Control Order, IS 17021 standards or prescribed gas chromatography dilution protocols.
Article Summary: Congress-led govt of Keralam Monday started collecting petrol samples to test whether their ethanol content was more than the prescribed 20%. This prompted Union minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi to say that states were free to conduct tests but they should avoid political mudslinging.

Article Title: 'Warrants urgent attention': SC flags vehicular pollution in Delhi-NCR, seeks action plan
Article Text:
Vehicles amid Delhi-NCR pollution

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has directed Delhi and three neighbouring states to detail the measures taken to prevent over-age and non-compliant vehicles from entering and operating in the National Capital Region (NCR), citing a sharp rise in vehicular emissions and calling for urgent intervention.The governments of Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan, along with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi and Delhi Police, have been asked to submit their responses within two weeks, outlining both existing enforcement measures and additional short-term and long-term steps to reduce vehicular pollution.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also sought details of the regulatory framework governing the entry and movement of commercial and private vehicles in Delhi-NCR, particularly those coming from neighbouring states.The authorities have been asked to explain how vehicles that do not meet prescribed emission standards are identified and regulated, including enforcement of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certification requirements.The court observed that Delhi-NCR bears the combined burden of vehicles originating within the region as well as those entering from neighbouring states. It also flagged the substantial volume of commercial and private vehicles adding to the pollution load."There can be little doubt that the issue warrants urgent and immediate intervention," the bench said, a squoted by PTI.The court also sought details of action taken against violations, including the number of vehicles inspected, challaned, denied entry or otherwise proceeded against. It asked the authorities to explain how Delhi and neighbouring states coordinate to regulate inter-state vehicular movement and ensure compliance with emission norms."The respective authorities shall also indicate the specific measures proposed to strengthen the existing enforcement mechanisms, together with a time-bound roadmap for their implementation," the bench said.The states have also been asked to respond to suggestions made by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and the amicus curiae, and spell out any additional measures they propose to take.The directions were issued on November 6 while the court was hearing a suo motu case on air pollution in Delhi-NCR. The bench noted that although stubble-burning incidents had declined substantially across Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan, the data also pointed to a sharp increase in concerns linked to vehicular emissions."While this development is certainly laudable, the same data also brings to the fore a converse and equally pressing concern, namely, the sharp increase in issues attributable to vehicular emissions," it said.The matter will be heard next on November 23.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has directed Delhi and three neighbouring states to detail the measures taken to prevent over-age and non-compliant vehicles from entering and operating in the National Capital Region. The governments of Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan, along with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi and Delhi Police, have been asked to submit their responses within two weeks.

Article Title: India, US plan joint crackdown on transnational drug cartels, synthetic drug trade
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a push to dismantle transnational narcotics syndicates, top security and policy officials from India and the United States convened in New Delhi for the 2nd India–US Drug Policy Executive Working Group Meeting. The high-level dialogue, hosted by India's Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) on November 2–3, aims to establish a synchronized framework to choke off synthetic drug flows, secure pharmaceutical supply chains, and cut off illicit drug financing across borders.Building on the foundational momentum of their inaugural January 2026 meeting in Washington, D.C., both nations used the two-day session to evaluate evolving trafficking trends and map out rigorous priorities for intelligence sharing, coordinated enforcement actions, precursor control, and demand reduction.The Indian delegation was led by NCB Director General Anurag Garg, while the US side was headed by Debbie Seguin, Acting Deputy Director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP).Opening the discussions, NCB Director General Garg spotlighted the India Vision Roadmap 2026–2029—formulated under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.Garg emphasized that India has transitioned to a robust, network-centric enforcement model designed to dismantle the entire illicit ecosystem by targeting kingpins, financiers, chemical suppliers, and logistical facilitators rather than street-level operatives alone.Underscoring the shared threat landscape, ONDCP Director and U.S. Drug Czar Sara Carter stressed that bilateral cooperation is vital to neutralizing transnational cartels that now operate like sophisticated multinational logistics enterprises.Referencing President Trump’s 2026 National Drug Control Strategy, Carter noted that countering these adaptive networks requires an equally targeted international response to secure commercial supply chains against chemical and pharmaceutical diversion.Amplifying the operational impact on the ground, U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor pointed to tangible results delivered by the partnership. Gor stated that both countries are actively choking off illicit precursor chemicals and dismantling cartels through high-trust, rapid law enforcement coordination that safeguards families in both nations.The meeting concluded with a mutual endorsement of key operational and regulatory milestones, including Operation MedMax, Operation WIPE, and India's Voluntary Code of Conduct designed to prevent the diversion of synthetic drug precursors.Both governments reaffirmed their long-term institutional commitment to regular intelligence exchanges, best-practice sharing, and comprehensive demand reduction initiatives.
Article Summary: The high-level dialogue aims to establish a synchronized framework to choke off synthetic drug flows, secure pharmaceutical supply chains, and cut off illicit drug financing across borders. The Indian delegation was led by NCB Director General Anurag Garg, while the US side was headed by Debbie Seguin, Acting Deputy Director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy.

Article Title: Adult vaccination remains low; elderly miss cover against flu and shingles
Article Text:
Adult vaccination remains low; elderly miss cover against flu and shingles

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Despite vaccines being available to prevent several infections that can be particularly serious for older people, adult immunisation remains low in India. Influenza, pneumococcal disease and shingles are among the key vaccine-preventable illnesses that pose a risk to older people, but studies point to poor awareness and low uptake of these vaccines. Ahead of World Immunisation Day Tuesday (Nov 10), the findings highlight a significant gap in protection beyond childhood.A multicentre study of 4,998 people aged 60 and above across Chennai, Ballabgarh, Kolkata and Pune found only 1.4% had ever received an influenza vaccine. While just 19.7% had heard of influenza, 35.9% considered vaccines safe and 65.3% were unwilling to pay for vaccination. However, uptake rose to 29.7% when vaccines were offered free of cost at community health camps.Published in 'BMC Public Health' in 2026, the study highlights gaps in awareness, acceptance and access to vaccination among older people.The disease burden is substantial. A separate study published in 'Influenza and Other Respiratory Viruses' in April 2026 estimated that influenza among Indians aged 60 and above accounted for 5.3 million respiratory infections, 36,149 hospitalisations and 84,613 deaths in 2021.The researchers found that an annual influenza vaccination programme for older adults could be cost-effective under most of the scenarios assessed."Influenza and pneumococcal infections cause a significant burden among older Indians, accounting for an estimated 1.2 lakh deaths annually. Studies show that influenza vaccination can reduce influenza-associated pneumonia cases by 52% and deaths by 70%, while pneumococcal vaccination can lower hospitalisations by around 27% and deaths by 34%. Yet vaccination coverage among the elderly remains very low," said Dr Neetu Jain, senior consultant, pulmonology, critical care and sleep medicine, PSRI Hospital."Annual flu and pneumococcal vaccination is particularly important for people above 60 and those with COPD, asthma, diabetes or heart disease, as infections can lead to serious complications, including respiratory failure and prolonged hospitalisation," she said.Evidence is also emerging of the economic value of pneumococcal vaccination. A study published in 'Infectious Diseases and Therapy' in Oct 2026 examined the cost-effectiveness of a single dose of the 20-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV20) for older adults and people at higher risk. It found that the vaccine could be a cost-effective option compared with existing vaccination approaches.Another infection of concern among older adults is shingles, caused by reactivation of the virus responsible for chicken pox. It can lead to prolonged nerve pain, known as post-herpetic neuralgia. A 2026 paper in 'Indian Journal of Community Medicine' noted the lack of robust population-based data on shingles in India, while citing an estimate of around 45 lakh cases annually. An Indian phase-3 trial of the recombinant zoster vaccine, published in 'Vaccine' in 2025, reported an immune response in 85.7% of participants aged 50 and above."Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines can reduce cases of severe illness, hospitalisation and complications, particularly among older people and those with chronic conditions such as diabetes, heart disease and COPD. Both are non-live vaccines and can be given to elderly people, including those with multiple conditions," said Dr Jatin Ahuja, infectious disease specialist, Apollo Hospitals, Delhi."India also needs to expand adult vaccination to cover shingles. The two-dose recombinant zoster vaccine is recommended for adults aged 50 and above and offers over 90% protection. Tdap or Td boosters, hepatitis B and, where indicated, Covid-19 and RSV vaccines should also be considered," he said.Goa has taken a step towards expanding vaccination beyond childhood through its Life-course Immunisation Policy 2026-2036, launched in Sept. The policy identifies influenza, pneumococcal and hepatitis B vaccination among its priorities for elderly, those with chronic illnesses, immunocompromised individuals and healthcare workers.
Article Summary: Influenza, pneumococcal disease and shingles are among the key vaccine- preventable illnesses that pose a risk to older people. Study of 4,998 people aged 60 and above across Chennai, Ballabgarh, Kolkata and Pune found 1.4% had ever received an influenza vaccine.

NEW DELHI: An Assam-based company was allegedly defrauded of more than Rs 11.5 crore by a gang posing as suppliers of goods to the Indian Army. The police arrested a 30-year-old man from Siliguri in West Bengal for his alleged role in masterminding the fraud.The accused, Harsh Agarwal, was arrested following an inter-state operation by a team from Guwahati's Panbazar Police Station. Police said they uncovered the alleged conspiracy through an investigation involving financial transactions, digital evidence and intelligence gathering. More than Rs 2 crore has so far been frozen in different bank accounts.According to police, the accused exploited an existing business relationship to gain the confidence of Global Traders, a Guwahati-based firm, news agency PTI reported. He allegedly used forged Indian Army supply orders, impersonated Army officers and produced fabricated financial documents to carry out the fraud.Investigators said Harsh introduced his brother, Ayush Agarwal, to the complainant as a distant relative involved in Army supply contracts. This helped the accused allegedly establish credibility and facilitate fraudulent transactions worth Rs 11,50,56,180.The case was cracked by a team led by Panbazar police station officer-in-charge Sankar Jyoti Nath. After identifying Harsh's alleged role, the team tracked him down to Siliguri and arrested him.The case has been registered at Panbazar Police Station under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act.Police said further investigation is underway to trace the defrauded money, identify other beneficiaries and arrest the remaining accused.

NEW DELHI: The Manipur high court has directed the Centre to keep the Census 2027 exercise in the state on hold until April 30, 2027, giving the authorities time to examine concerns raised over conducting the population count amid the continuing impact of ethnic violence and displacement.A division bench of Justices M Sundar and A Guneshwar Sharma asked the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India to consider seven representations on the issue and pass a reasoned order by April 30 next year. The existing notifications suspending the exercise will remain in force until then."To put it differently, the census exercise for the State of Manipur will continue to be put on hold/kept in abeyance till 30.04.2027," the Bench said as per Bar and Bench.The court also ordered that the Census remain suspended for four weeks after the authorities take a decision on the representations. This period will allow anyone aggrieved by the decision to challenge it before the court.The November 4 order came on a public interest litigation filed by the Kangleipak Students' Association (KSA) and International Peace and Social Advancement (IPSA), along with a separate petition filed by Shanta Singh Nahakpam.The petitioners argued that conducting the Census while thousands of people remained displaced by ethnic violence could affect the accuracy of population records. They also raised concerns about identifying internally displaced persons and accounting for their circumstances before carrying out the exercise.The proceedings also referred to resolutions unanimously adopted by the Manipur Legislative Assembly on August 5, 2022, and March 1, 2024, calling for the introduction and enforcement of the National Register of Citizens (NRC).During earlier hearings, the petitioners had asked the court to postpone the Census until their concerns were addressed.On August 31, the Centre informed the High Court that it had decided to defer house-listing operations for Census 2027 in Manipur. The state government also assured the court that it would not begin the exercise scheduled for September 1, 2026.Following this, the Registrar General and Census Commissioner issued notifications on September 5 and October 30 regarding the postponement. The court took note of these steps and observed that the parties agreed that the representations should be examined before the Census could proceed.The Bench directed the Census Commissioner to assess all seven representations on their merits and issue a common, reasoned order. It also allowed individuals and organisations, including the petitioners, to submit further representations until November 25, 2026.The authorities may also hold public consultations to consider the concerns raised. If they decide against holding such consultations, they will have to provide reasons for doing so.The court further directed that the final decision be communicated to the petitioners' lawyers within five working days and uploaded to the official websites of the Manipur government and the Census Commissioner.Those dissatisfied with the decision will be free to approach the High Court, which will consider their grievances independently."Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the nature of the matter, larger public interest and national interest involved, this Court deems it appropriate to place on record its appreciation for all counsel, senior counsel, learned Advocate General and learned DSGI for taking a very fair and balanced approach to the matter without treating the same like a regular adversarial legal drill," the Bench as per Bar and Bench.
Article Summary: The Manipur high court has directed the Centre to keep the Census 2027 exercise in the state on hold until April 30, 2027. A division bench of Justices M Sundar and A Guneshwar Sharma asked the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India to consider seven representations on the issue.

Article Title: Karnataka, Keralam governments launch E20 petrol quality checks amid ethanol blending concerns
Article Text:
The Keralam civil supplies department conducted inspections of petrol pumps in Kochi to examine the ethanol mix in E20 petrol. (Pic Credit: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Keralam civil supplies department has inspected petrol pumps in Kochi to verify the ethanol content and density of E20 petrol amid growing concerns over alleged excessive ethanol blending in fuel.District civil supplies Officer Shaji PR said officials had collected six one-litre petrol samples during the inspection, of which two were sent to an analytical chemical laboratory in Kakinada for testing. The department is awaiting the laboratory reports."We conducted an inspection... We have inspected the details of the quantity of ethanol in the motor spirit, ordinary petrol. There were six samples at the rate of one litre taken. We sent two samples to an analytical chemical laboratory in Kakinada. We are waiting for the result," Shaji PR told ANI.The inspections come amid concerns raised by Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad over the possible impact of higher ethanol-blended petrol on vehicles. On Friday, he warned that fuel containing more than 20 per cent ethanol could damage vehicle components that are not designed to withstand higher concentrations.Addressing a press conference on November 6, Arshad said the Karnataka government had collected 63 fuel samples from different locations across every district, covering all major oil companies.The issue has also drawn criticism from Leader of opposition in the Lok sabha Rahul Gandhi, who questioned the centre over allegations that petrol sold in Karnataka contained ethanol beyond the prescribed 20 per cent limit. He sought to know when action would be taken against oil companies allegedly supplying fuel with excessive ethanol content.In a post on X, Gandhi described the alleged irregularity as an 'E20' scam, writing: "E20 turns into '420' (a scam) petrol theft from the public's vehicles. The Modi government claims that petrol contains 20% ethanol. The Karnataka government collected petrol samples from 7 districts and had them tested at an accredited laboratory."Karnataka's department of food, civil supplies, consumer affairs and legal metrology has claimed that motor spirit sold at certain retail outlets in the state contained ethanol concentrations ranging from 26 per cent to 31 per cent.However, the union ministry of petroleum and natural gas has rejected allegations of excessive ethanol blending, stating that all 893 samples of E20 petrol collected from public sector oil marketing companies across 27 states and Union Territories met the prescribed quality standards.The three state-run oil marketing companies, Indian oil corporation limited, Bharat petroleum corporation limited and Hindustan petroleum corporation limited, have also maintained that ethanol blending is a regulated and automated process carried out in accordance with statutory guidelines, rather than through manual intervention.
Article Summary: The Keralam civil supplies department has inspected petrol pumps in Kochi to verify the ethanol content and density of E20 petrol. The inspections come amid concerns raised by Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad over the possible impact of higher ethanol-blended petrol on vehicles.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang loses $7.4 billion in 30 minutes, drops 2 spots in Forbes rich list
Article Text:
The investigation follows a report by The New York Times last month that US intelligence agencies had identified a close relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen suspected by Washington of gathering information for Beijing.

Allegation against Alice Huang

A photo shows NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang with a woman confirmed by a Reuters source to be Alice Huang in Taipei, Taiwan released on June 7, 2024.

Trump defends Nvidia chief

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife Lori Huang attend the 12th Breakthrough Prize ceremony gala in Santa Monica, California, US on April 18

What lies ahead for Nvidia

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang slipped to 10th place on Forbes’ list of the world’s richest people after his net worth plunged by $7.4 billion on Monday. The drop followed a sharp fall in the company’s share price amid an investigation into his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.Huang’s net worth dropped from $162.2 billion to $154.7 billion within the first half-hour of trading, pushing him down two places from number 8 to number 10 in the Forbes real-time billionaire rankings, according to a report by Forbes. He briefly fell out of the top 10 after Nvidia shares opened more than 7 per cent lower, wiping out $10.3 billion from his fortune.Also Read | Nvidia's billionaire boss has admitted to cheating on his wife. Was he the target of Chinese spying? Nvidia shares were down 5.5 per cent at 1.30pm EST, after falling as much as 7 per cent in premarket trading. This was the first trading session since the company confirmed an investigation into Huang. The development also put him below Berkshire Hathaway chairman Warren Buffett and Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison in the billionaire rankings.The fall in Nvidia shares also hit the company's market value. Its market capitalisation dropped from $4.5 trillion. Nvidia has frequently competed with Apple for the position of the world's most valuable publicly traded company.The share price decline followed Huang's admission on Sunday that he had an affair. In a statement to employees, he apologised for his actions and said he supported the company's investigation.Nvidia's board said it had appointed a committee of independent directors, along with external legal counsel, to examine all available information. However, it added that it had "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised."The investigation follows a report by The New York Times last month that US intelligence agencies had identified a close relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen suspected by Washington of gathering information for Beijing.According to The New York Times, Alice Huang was recruited by Beijing's top spy agency to collect information on Jensen Huang for China's ministry of state security. The report cited a memo circulated within the Trump administration.It remains unclear when the two first met. However, they were photographed together at a bar in June 2024.Alice Huang has also reportedly had connections with other artificial intelligence chip industry leaders, including executives at Gigabyte, a company that assembles Nvidia supercomputers.She has described herself as the chief executive of Singapore-based neocloud and AI computing services provider Megaspeed. However, the company removed her as managing director from its official paperwork after the first eight months, according to The New York Times.Megaspeed was established in 2023 after Chinese gaming and cloud computing company 7Road spun off its overseas operations in Singapore. The company partners with Nvidia and supplies its technology across the Asia-Pacific region.US authorities have been investigating the company's possible role in China's access to Nvidia chips since 2024. A Commerce Department official had found Nvidia equipment still packed in boxes at a data centre site in Malaysia, raising concerns that it could be shipped elsewhere.Also Read| What Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang first told the world about Alice Huang, the woman he has admitted having an affair with US intelligence officials had briefed President Donald Trump about their findings concerning Alice Huang around a year ago, The New York Times reported. However, Trump did not take action at the time.An Nvidia spokesperson had earlier told the newspaper that "Jensen’s interactions with Ms Huang are not unusual or unexpected," adding that meeting customers was part of his job.Huang has also emerged as an ally and technology adviser to Trump. The US president rolled back restrictions introduced by the Biden administration in 2022 to limit global exports of advanced AI chips.Trump defended the Nvidia chief on Sunday night, calling him an "honorable guy". He also said he would still include Huang in his upcoming visit to China.The investigation comes at a crucial time for Nvidia, which is scheduled to announce its quarterly earnings next Tuesday after the market closes.The company's second-quarter results showed its data centre business generating $89 billion in revenue, up 117 per cent year-on-year. The segment accounted for around 92 per cent of Nvidia's total revenue for the quarter, while overall revenue stood at $96.2 billion, beating expectations.Nvidia was also the only company among the so-called Magnificent Seven, a group comprising Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Meta and Tesla, to record a premarket decline on Monday.

He briefly fell out of the top 10 after Nvidia shares opened more than 7 per cent lower, wiping out $10.3 billion from his fortune. The share price decline followed Huang's admission on Sunday that he had an affair.
