Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $200 million Six Flags investment faces $279 dining pass lawsuit as frustrated customers demand long-overdue refunds
Article Text:
Travis Kelce(Image via Getty Images)

Travis Kelce's Six Flags connection draws attention amid refund controversy

Six Flags and Enchanted Parks face class-action lawsuit over refunds

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Travis Kelce has helped Six Flags attract attention with his star power and financial backing. However, the amusement park giant is now facing an uncomfortable situation as customers demand answers over money they say they are still owed. A new class-action lawsuit involving Six Flags and Enchanted Parks has brought the company's customer service problems into focus. The dispute centres on dining plans that became invalid after a change in park ownership, leaving families waiting months for refunds. With Kelce connected to the company as both an investor and brand ambassador, the controversy adds another layer of interest.Travis Kelce's relationship with Six Flags goes beyond a promotional partnership. In October 2025, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end joined investment firm Jana Partners and other business executives in an investment group that acquired a collective economic interest of approximately 9% in Six Flags Entertainment. The group wanted to encourage changes that could improve the company's value and guest experience.The following March, Six Flags announced Kelce as its brand ambassador for 2026.His role included supporting marketing campaigns, creating digital content and promoting the company's amusement parks across North America.The partnership made sense given Kelce's childhood connection to amusement parks. However, the latest lawsuit puts the company's guest experience under a different kind of spotlight.The dispute began after Enchanted Parks acquired Six Flags St. Louis in April 2026. The new operator announced that previously purchased dining plans would no longer be accepted. Customers could request refunds or choose an alternative, but several reportedly struggled to receive their money.One customer, Sonya Parrent, has now taken legal action alongside her attorney, Christopher Roberts. Parrent paid $279 for dining plans for her family and said she had been waiting six months for a refund.She recalled receiving a message promising payment within three to five business days in August. However, the money never arrived.Roberts believes thousands of customers may have faced similar problems. He explained, “What happened is that Sonya, and we believe thousands of customers, kind of got left behind. They purchased these meal plans, which are actually significantly more expensive than the season passes, and they didn’t get anything in return,”The attorney also questioned why customers had to choose between a refund and a gift card within a limited period. He believes all affected dining plan holders deserve their money back, along with interest.Six Flags acknowledged the frustration and said most eligible refunds had been processed. Its statement added:“We recognize the frustration of Enchanted Parks guests who submitted Dining Plan refund requests and appreciate their continued patience. Most eligible refunds have been processed, and we are committed to working through individual cases where the original refund attempt was unsuccessful.”Enchanted Parks had not responded to First Alert 4's request for comment at the time of publication.Meanwhile, Parrent remains unhappy with the company's response. She said Enchanted Parks offered her a discount on a season pass for next year, but questioned the offer while her refund remained unresolved.“Now you want me to spend more money with you, and you haven’t even given me a refund,” responded Parrent.For Six Flags, the lawsuit raises questions about how the ownership transition was handled. With Kelce serving as a prominent face of the brand and part of its investor group, the company's ability to restore customer confidence could become an important part of its next chapter.
Article Summary: Six Flags and Enchanted Parks face class-action lawsuit over refunds. The dispute centres on dining plans that became invalid after a change in park ownership. With Travis Kelce connected to the company as both an investor and brand ambassador, the controversy adds another layer of interest.

Article Title: Nvidia shares drop after CEO Jensen Huang admits affair with suspected Chinese spy; what it means for company
Article Text:
Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife but did not provide details about the relationship.

Jensen Huang & the 'Chinese spy' scandal

Impact on Nvidia and its shares

Nvidia shares declined in after-hours trading on Monday following the announcement of an internal investigation to find out if the company’s chief executive Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The investigation has raised questions about Jensen Huang’s future at the AI chipmaker which is among the most valuable listed companies in the world.Announced on Sunday, the investigation has drawn attention to Huang's position at Nvidia, the world's most valuable chipmaker. His future is also under scrutiny because of his prominent role as one of the leading salesmen of the artificial intelligence boom.Jensen Huang, 63, has headed Nvidia since he established the company in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. His long tenure makes him one of Silicon Valley's longest-serving chief executives among company founders.Born in Taiwan and brought up in the US, Huang emerged as a key figure in the artificial intelligence revolution. He steered Nvidia from its original business of manufacturing graphics chips for video games to becoming the world's leading supplier of AI processors.The company launched the internal inquiry following a media report alleging that Huang had a close association with a Chinese businesswoman who had allegedly shared information with Beijing.In a message to Nvidia employees, Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife but did not provide details about the relationship.The New York Times reported last month that Huang had been involved in a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is not related to him. US authorities investigated Alice Huang and concluded that she was an asset of Chinese intelligence.Megaspeed's website identifies the company as an Nvidia Cloud Partner in the Asia-Pacific region. It also lists Nvidia's GB200 NVL72 and HGX H100 chips among the products it offers.The developments also had repercussions in South Korea. Madison Huang, Jensen Huang's daughter and an Nvidia executive, called off a scheduled visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference due to begin on Monday, according to companies that had been due to meet her.Madison Huang had been scheduled to visit South Korean artificial intelligence startup Rebellions and participate in a question-and-answer session with Kakao Mobility. Rebellions said both engagements had been called off because of "unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia."South Korean media reported that Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day conference expected to attract around 2,000 participants, would go ahead as scheduled. The event is set to focus on physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.According to a Reuters report, trading in perpetual futures on the Hyperliquid exchange, along with after-hours share transactions on the Blue Ocean system, indicated that Nvidia shares were changing hands at around $178.60. This is a decline of more than 4% from the stock's closing price of $186.64 on the Nasdaq on Friday.Nvidia's chip technology has played a central role in several major shifts in the technology industry, spanning video gaming, autonomous vehicles, cloud computing and artificial intelligence.Huang's early decision to invest in AI proved significant. By the time ChatGPT was launched in late 2022, Nvidia's processors were already central to the computing infrastructure needed to meet the rapidly growing demand for AI applications.The company's market value has since climbed sharply, making it one of the world's most valuable businesses and an essential supplier to leading technology companies. Nvidia's valuation rose from $420 billion in late 2022 to $4.5 trillion as of November 6."The market's probably telling you now this does no favours ⁠to the stock whatsoever in a time when there's a lot of conjecture as to the build out of data centres," Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne told Reuters.However, Weston said he did not expect Huang, whom he described as the "godfather of AI", to be replaced."If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down — it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest,” he said.The scrutiny of Huang's relationship with Alice Huang has emerged at a sensitive point for Nvidia. Investors are already questioning whether the AI boom that fuelled the company's extraordinary growth can be sustained. The board's investigation has added another layer of uncertainty by raising questions about the future of the executive most closely linked to Nvidia's success.The issue has also drawn attention from senior Republicans in the US House of Representatives, who have sought briefings from Huang following The New York Times report, pointing to concerns over national security.Nvidia has maintained that its board has "no reason to believe" that US national security or company secrets were compromised. However, an independent committee of directors will examine all the information available as part of its review.Analysts cautioned that an extended investigation or internal review could affect Nvidia's investment decisions and product launches, potentially creating wider repercussions for the semiconductor industry.Ryu Young-ho, a senior analyst at NH Investment & Securities, said competitors such as Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) could receive increased attention in the near term. This could also bring Samsung into greater focus because of its close business ties ⁠with AMD.However, Ryu said Nvidia's products would be difficult to replace, which could limit the overall impact of the developments. He added that shipments to China might face further delays, depending on how the situation unfolded.South Korea's deputy science minister said on Monday that the government did not expect any disruption to deliveries of Nvidia graphics processing units covered by existing contracts, despite the challenges currently confronting the company.Shares of Nvidia's major Asian chip suppliers recovered on Monday following last week's selloff in AI-related stocks. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) rose 6.5%, while Samsung Electronics gained 2.9% and SK Hynix advanced 4.7%.Several prominent personalities also commented on Huang's admission. Billionaire investor Bill Ackman, who founded Pershing Square Capital Management, described the Nvidia chief executive as an "incredible human" in a post on X. However, he added that ‌if "indeed this is ⁠more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem.""I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security," he added.Tesla CEO Elon Musk responded with "I agree" to a post by Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire. Maguire had said Huang "did something incredibly dumb" that was "bad for America", while also maintaining that "Jensen is irreplaceable for America's AI leadership".US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he had not discussed the allegations with Huang. He nevertheless described the Nvidia CEO as a fine person. "I hope everything's fine. He's done such an incredible job," he added.Asked whether he believed he should have acted on the intelligence after being briefed about it, Trump said: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for ⁠it. You have to hear it."The New York Times reported that Trump had been briefed on the intelligence findings approximately a year ago but decided against taking action based on the information.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife but did not provide details about the relationship. The New York Times reported last month that Huang had been involved in a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed. US authorities investigated Alice Huang and concluded that she was an asset of Chinese intelligence.

Article Title: HSBC upgrades Indian equities to 'overweight', downgrades Chinese stocks to 'neutral'
Article Text:
HSBC upgrades Indian equities

Banks, industrials and discretionary consumption among preferred bets

China loses overweight status

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market and other asset classes given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

NEW DELHI: India's prolonged stock market correction appears to have made its equities more attractive to global investors, with HSBC raising its rating on the market to 'overweight' from 'neutral'. The global financial services firm cited resilient earnings, improving growth prospects and a reset in valuations as reasons behind its more positive stance.In its latest Asia-Pacific equity strategy report, HSBC said India's investment appeal is supported by strong credit growth, improving earnings momentum and policy measures aimed at sustaining economic growth and currency stability.A key factor behind the upgrade is the correction in Indian equity valuations over several years. HSBC said this reset has made valuations more reasonable, particularly among large-cap stocks, after a period in which Indian markets underperformed other emerging markets.There could also be room for more foreign investment in Indian equities. According to the report, just 22 per cent of global emerging market (GEM) funds currently have an overweight position in India, suggesting scope for further allocations.The brokerage also pointed to the resilience of corporate earnings despite challenging macroeconomic conditions."Growth remains resilient despite a series of macro shocks (i.e., higher interest rates and oil)," the report said, adding that the pace of earnings downgrades has become significantly more modest.Another factor supporting India's appeal is its relatively low volatility and the diversification it offers. HSBC said these characteristics are particularly relevant in Asian markets, where artificial intelligence-related stocks are increasingly dominating investment opportunities.HSBC's preferred sectors reflect its positive assessment of India's growth prospects. Banks remain among its favoured segments, with the brokerage pointing to an improved growth outlook.In the industrial space, it identified capital goods, cement, ports and electronic manufacturing services as areas offering opportunities.The brokerage also drew a distinction between consumer discretionary stocks and staples, expressing a preference for the former. Retailers and automobile companies were among its preferred segments within this category.Insurers and hospitals also remained on HSBC's positive list, with the firm highlighting their growth potential despite recent regulatory uncertainties.However, the outlook is not without risks. HSBC flagged elevated crude oil prices and the possibility of an El Niño weather pattern as potential challenges for the Indian economy.The report warned that if energy prices remain high, they could put pressure on domestic demand and the currency. Higher inflation could also weigh on consumption, with rural demand particularly vulnerable.Even so, HSBC does not expect possible earnings downgrades in the coming quarters to be large enough to significantly undermine overall market sentiment.While HSBC has become more positive on India, its assessment of Chinese equities has turned cautious. The brokerage cut its rating on China to 'neutral' from 'overweight', citing a lack of triggers for a sustained improvement in market valuations.This comes despite attractive valuations and recent policy support. HSBC said weak consumer confidence, persistent difficulties in the property market and softer domestic investment continue to pose challenges to China's growth outlook.Investor activity also points to weaker appetite for Chinese equities. The report highlighted subdued southbound investment flows and declining margin financing, while noting that there are no clear signs of meaningful near-term policy support to strengthen underlying economic growth."Our downgrade reflects our belief that there are limited catalysts that can drive a sustained re-rating," the report said.Despite the downgrade, HSBC continues to see opportunities in select Chinese sectors. Its preferences include banks, consumer stocks offering attractive bond yields, biotechnology and technology hardware companies expected to benefit from the rollout of artificial intelligence.
Article Summary: HSBC raises its rating on the market to 'overweight' from 'neutral' The global financial services firm cited resilient earnings, improving growth prospects and a reset in valuations as reasons behind its more positive stance. Just 22 per cent of global emerging market (GEM) funds currently have an overweight position in India.

NEW DELHI: Social media is flooded with screenshots of some apps showing Delhi's AQI touching 1,500 to 1,800 on Diwali night even as the city's official AQI shared by the Central Pollution Control Board remains below 400.While CPCB has capped Delhi's AQI at 500, other apps, which follow the US's Environmental Protection Agency and WHO's methodology, have no such bar. TOI explains the breakpoint tables of methodologiesCPCB (India): 373IAQIR (Swiss firm, uses US method): 214AQI Live-US (Also has India option): 1,747CPCB: 360IAQIR: 163AQI Live-US: 217The Air Quality Index is determined by monitoring the levels of major air pollutants, such as:For each pollutant, set limits—called breakpoints—help convert its measured level into an AQI score and category.0–50 (Good) | 100 | 200 | 300 | 400–500 (Severe): 0–50 (Good) | 100 | 150 | 200 | 300–500 (HazardouS)India calculates using 24-hr averages, while others use shorter/longer timeframes like hourly avg.For Good, the upper concentration limits are compared. For Severe/Hazardous, comparison is for the concentrations at which those categories begin. Percentages are rounded.A lower threshold means the AQI category is reached at a lower pollutant concentration.Only the 'Good' and 'Severe/Hazardous' categories of the six-category AQI systems are compared for illustrative purposes.: India uses a 24-hour average; the US uses a 1-hour average. Article Title: Rs 3-crore Defender, horse race with SUV prize, 150 dishes: Anant Singh goes all out for daughter's wedding
Article Text:
Mokama MLA Anant Singh is ensuring his daughter’s big day will be difficult to miss.





PATNA: A Rs 3-crore Land Rover Defender for the bridegroom, a BMW worth around Rs 1 crore for the younger son, a wedding venue spread over more than 10 bighas, a horse race with an SUV as the top prize and a menu boasting over 150 dishes.If weddings are about making a statement, Mokama MLA Anant Singh is ensuring his daughter’s big day will be difficult to miss. Add Bollywood and Bhojpuri artists, six models from Dubai and invitations for some of the country’s biggest political names, and the celebrations in Ladma village have become an event with all eyes on it.Known for his flamboyant lifestyle and larger-than-life public persona, Singh is preparing for the Nov 25 wedding of his younger daughter, Shivangi Singh , to Rishikesh Kumar alias Ankit, son of commandant Ranvijay Kumar of Krishnanagar in Bihta, Patna. Rishikesh holds an MBA degree and has lived in the United States for around 11 years.The luxury Defender, estimated to cost between Rs 2.5 crore and Rs 3 crore, has already reached Ladma. The BMW, worth around Rs 1 crore, is for Singh’s youngest son Abhinav, whose ‘janeu’ ceremony will be held alongside the wedding. The vehicles have become a talking point in the village even before the wedding festivities have gathered full pace.The wedding venue is being developed across more than 10 bighas, while a separate ground spread over nearly 12 bighas is being prepared for the horse-racing competition. The scale of the arrangements has prompted Singh to plan for around four lakh visitors, with preparations allowing for the possibility of even more guests.The wedding decorations are being planned on a similarly imposing scale. A nearly 30-foot-high stage, inspired by Jaipur’s Patrakar Chauraha, is being built for the ‘jaimala’ ceremony. Flowers are being sourced from China and Bengaluru, decorative materials from different parts of the country, and tent workers have been brought in from Mau in Uttar Pradesh. A specialised event company has been entrusted with the work.Puneet Kumar, Singh’s eldest son-in-law, said the Defender was chosen by Shivangi and gifted to her on her birthday. She completed her schooling in Delhi and post-graduation from Delhi University.The family has a history of elaborate wedding arrangements. “I was married to Raj Nandini, eldest daughter of Singh, in 2015. In my wedding, only parking was made on around 4 bighas of land,” said the son-in-law.The horse race, scheduled for Nov 25 from 2pm to 4pm, is expected to draw riders from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana and other states. Manish Kumar, an associate of Singh, said the winner would receive an SUV, the runner-up a motorcycle and the third-place finisher a scooter.Food, too, is being treated as an event in itself. The menu will feature more than 150 varieties, ranging from traditional Bihari preparations to dishes from other states. Sweets will include kaju katli and Silao khaja, the Nalanda speciality known for its distinctive 52-layer structure.Singh has also expressed his wish to invite PM Narendra Modi , former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, RJD president Lalu Prasad and Tejashwi Prasad Yadav. Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar has already received an invitation.Singh, who has been asked by the Supreme Court to surrender on Dec 4 in Dularchand murder case, has said there will be no political distinction among guests and visitors from anywhere in the world, including India and Pakistan, will be welcome.

Article Title: Crackers versus vehicles: What really contributes to Delhi's Diwali pollution?
Article Text:
Vehicles and transport emissions contributed 19% to Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution on the day of the festival, November 8

Diwali fireworks add to existing pollution

Vehicles: An endless source

Diwali fireworks release fine particles that rapidly worsen air quality

Crackers push particulate levels sharply higher

Low wind speeds and temperature inversion make it harder to disperse pollutants

What crackers bring to the table

Delhi's PM2

Weather is the difference

Can't ignore either one





Every year, Delhi’s Diwali pollution debate is between two sources: firecrackers and vehicles. But the latest pollution data suggests the problem is more complex. Pollution can spike sharply in the case of fireworks, but vehicles are one of the biggest contributors to the city’s everyday PM2.5 burden.The real worry is what will happen when these emissions combine with an atmosphere that is already polluted and with bad weather.The Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) has set up a new Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory (AATAL), which gives a useful picture of Delhi’s pollution mix.Vehicles were the single largest contributor to the city’s PM2.5 pollution on Oct. 24, accounting for 25%. Secondary organic aerosols contributed 18.4 %, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols (16.5 %), road dust (10.9 %) and waste burning (5 %).Even around Diwali the transport contribution was still substantial. Vehicles and transport emissions contributed 19% to Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution on the day of the festival, November 8, the largest identified source, estimated the IITM’s Decision Support System (DSS).The figure explains why vehicular pollution cannot be seen as a seasonal problem: unlike fireworks, traffic emissions persist throughout the year.But firecrackers cause pollution of a different kind of episode. They tend to emit their emissions over a relatively short period of time, and they emit fine particles and gasses that can quickly degrade air quality.The effect was visible on the night of Diwali. The Delhi Pollution Control Committee’s data reported on November 9 showed that at Akshardham the PM2.5 concentration was at 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11pm. This was an hourly reading, not a 24 hour average, but gives an idea of how intense the spike of pollution was.Delhi’s AQI had already fallen to 382 on November 6, its worst pre-Diwali reading in eight years, according to CPCB data. It averaged 376 on Diwali November 8, from 369 a day earlier. AQI stood at 368 at 7am on November 9. Of the 54 monitoring stations that reported valid readings, 50 were above 300 and 15 entered the severe category.At the time when fireworks are set off, the Delhi atmosphere is becoming less conducive to dispersing pollutants. The Air Quality Early Warning System said dispersion is difficult when ventilation index is less than 6,000 square meters per second and average wind speeds are below 10kmph. Low temperatures and temperature inversion can also trap pollutants near the ground.That means fireworks smoke doesn’t just disappear when the party’s over. It adds to the existing emissions from vehicles, industry, dust and regional sources, thus adding to the particulate load.The latest figures do not allow for simply blaming either crackers or vehicles. Fireworks are a concentrated blast of pollution to an already stressed atmosphere, but cars carry the burden of emissions daily. Cracker restrictions can curb the festive spike, but sustained improvement will depend on curbing transport emissions, controlling road dust and industrial pollution, and improving regional coordination. One night of action cannot fix a year-long problem of air pollution in Delhi.
Article Summary: Vehicles were the single largest contributor to the city’s PM2.5 pollution on Oct. 24, accounting for 25%. Secondary organic aerosols contributed 18.4 %, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols (16.5%) and road dust (10.9%) Fireworks are a concentrated blast of pollution to an already stressed atmosphere, but cars carry the burden of emissions daily.

Article Title: Samsung set to become South Korea's first company with 200 trillion won in cash
Article Text:
Samsung's cash reserves to cross 200 trillion won as AI chip demand grows

Samsung Electronics is on course to become the first company in South Korea to build cash assets of more than 200 trillion won ($146.6 billion), with the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven semiconductor boom strengthening its financial position.The chipmaker's cash reserves have nearly doubled over the past year, while its overall assets have also grown. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. This marks a rise of 24.8 trillion won from the 190 trillion won recorded at the end of the previous quarter, as reported by Yonhap news agency.The latest estimate is also almost twice the 108.5 trillion won the company held at the end of the third quarter of 2025.Samsung's total assets stood at 791.8 trillion won at the end of September, an increase of 32.4 trillion won over the preceding three months.The company's growing cash position is expected to be enough to cover the highest possible payout under its landmark shareholder return policy announced in August, market watchers estimate.Samsung had indicated that it would make between 90 trillion won and 110 trillion won available for shareholder returns in 2026.The company is also expected to announce its shareholder policy for the coming year at a board meeting scheduled for January.Alongside shareholder payouts, Samsung is preparing for a significant increase in spending on its semiconductor business.Investments in chipmaking infrastructure and research and development are expected to exceed 100 trillion won this year, marking a historic high. Of this amount, 84.4 trillion won is expected to go towards expanding its memory production facilities.Samsung expects the semiconductor supercycle to extend through next year, supported by continued investments in artificial intelligence and a crunch in memory supply.
Article Summary: Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.

Article Title: Rupee extends winning streak, breaks below 94 against dollar: What's next
Article Text:
Rupee moves below 94 against US dollar

Crude oil prices cool as hopes of peace grow

Foreign fund inflows add to rupee's support

NEW DELHI: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East.The currency rose 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade. It opened at around 93.85 in the interbank forex market before gaining further. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98 against the greenback.Forex traders said rupee could maintain its positive momentum if diplomatic efforts in the Middle East make progress. Any easing of tensions could reduce the risk premium in crude oil prices, providing further support to the currency.These hopes gained ground over the weekend after US President Donald Trump indicated that further military strikes against Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed and both sides reached a strong agreement.The easing in crude oil prices has been one of the key factors supporting rupee. Brent crude, which had earlier climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. Amit Pabari, managing director of CR Forex Advisors, said improving diplomatic expectations were already having an impact on energy prices."The improvement in diplomatic expectations is already reflecting in energy prices. Brent crude, which had climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. For currency markets, even the possibility of a lasting agreement is important," Pabari said.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.15% lower at $98.17 per barrel in futures trade. The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was also down 0.12% at 102.18.Foreign investment activity provided another source of support for the domestic currency. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.The combination of lower crude prices and stronger foreign fund inflows has supported the rupee's recent gains against the dollar.With rupee now below the 94-per-dollar level, Pabari sees further room for appreciation. He expects the currency to move towards 93.50 and 93.00, while identifying 94.40–94.50 as the immediate resistance zone."With USD/INR breaking below the 94.00 mark, the probability of further rupee appreciation towards 93.50 and 93.00 has increased. On the upside, 94.40–94.50 is likely to act as the immediate resistance zone," Pabari said.Meanwhile, domestic equity markets opened lower on Monday. BSE Sensex fell 93.95 points to 80,919.19, while NSE Nifty declined 30 points to 24,968.80.Separately, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion in the week ended October 30.
Article Summary: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98.

Article Title: Research claims that many companies in the US are calling back employees they fired and replaced by AI; and it is costing them more, as sacked employees now …
Article Text:
Areas where companies are finding AI falls short

Klarna and Ford adjust course

AI layoffs continue to climb

Nearly one in five US workers say they have experienced a surprising workplace reversal: their employer replaced them with artificial intelligence (AI), only to ask them to come back later, a report has found. According to new research from talent assessment firm SHL, this growing trend – which the firm calls “AI rebounding” – suggests several companies are learning the hard way that AI cannot do everything human employees can. And bringing those workers back is proving expensive.The SHL survey, conducted in June and July, and published recently, found that 19.1% of US respondents had been replaced by AI and subsequently asked to return to their jobs. Across both the US and the UK, that figure stood at 16%. However, those returning workers are not coming back on the old terms.According to SHL:51% demanded a substantial pay increase before agreeing to return.42% required written guarantees about their future job security.40% wanted clear transparency on how AI would be used in their roles.“Organisations are making fast, sometimes myopic, decisions about their people based on an incomplete picture of what their employees can do with or without AI.AI rebounding is what happens when a company automates a role before it has genuinely assessed the human capability inside it. The AI doesn’t deliver, the gap becomes obvious, and the business ends up rehiring the same experts they just let go of, at a far greater cost,” said Lucy Beaumont, global senior vice president of product and design at SHL, in a press release.SHL’s findings line up with a separate July survey from Robert Half. That study found that 32% of US hiring managers whose companies cut jobs because of AI eventually had to bring back the same or similar positions. Among those hiring managers, the gaps left by automation were clear:40% said the roles required institutional knowledge or context that AI could not replicate.39% cited relationship management.39% pointed to increased business demand.38% said the jobs needed more human oversight and quality control than the company expected.Several major companies have already run into these limits firsthand. For example, Swedish buy-now, pay-later firm Klarna recently began hiring human customer service representatives again after leaning heavily on AI chatbots.CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski acknowledged the company had gone too far with automation, Bloomberg reported. A Klarna spokesperson told Fortune that human agents were necessary “for complex, sensitive cases,” noting the company was directly hiring a “small number” of high-skilled workers to see where the “human touch” adds the most value.Similarly, automaker Ford made a move in June, hiring and promoting 350 experienced engineers after AI-powered quality control tools fell short of expectations. While Ford noted that AI has helped improve quality, a company representative told Fortune that “these engineers carry the hard-earned wisdom of decades of design,” adding that pairing AI with deep technical expertise is what actually gets results.Even as some employers backtrack, overall AI-driven job cuts are still rising sharply.As per the data from outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas, employers cited AI in 121,401 announced job cuts through October. That is already more than double the 54,836 AI-related layoffs announced during all of 2025. The report also said younger workers are taking the brunt of the shift. A study from the Stanford Digital Economy Lab found that employment among workers aged 22 to 25 in jobs heavily exposed to AI was 19% lower than it would have been if it had grown at the same pace as less-exposed fields.
Article Summary: 19.1% of US respondents had been replaced by AI and subsequently asked to return to their jobs. Across both the US and the UK, that figure stood at 16%. However, those returning workers are not coming back on the old terms.

Article Title: In 2024, Jeff Bezos paid $87 million for a third mansion on Miami's Billionaire Bunker; he and Lauren Sánchez Bezos transformed the temporary home with exotic gardens, a private gym and a pickleball c
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos' three mansions worth $234 million on Billionaire Bunker

Bezos and Lauren Sánchez's plans for a mega-mansion

Exotic trees and private gardens reshape the mansion's grounds

A private pickleball court and an expanded poolside dining area

The mansion's garage has been converted into a private gym

Bezos' move to Florida brought a different property chapter

Indian Creek is one part of Bezos' extensive property portfolio

Disclaimer: This article is based on information publicly available. The Times of India has not independently verified the property details, purchase prices, renovation costs, reported improvements or future development plans mentioned. The information should not be interpreted as confirmation from Jeff Bezos, Lauren Sánchez Bezos or their representatives.

Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos may eventually move into a sprawling custom-built estate on Florida's exclusive Indian Creek Island, but their plans for the property have not stopped them from upgrading the house they currently call home. According to the Realtor, the Amazon founder paid $87 million for a third mansion on the island in 2024, adding to two neighbouring properties he had already acquired the previous year. What was expected to serve as temporary accommodation has since become the subject of an extensive renovation. From carefully planted tropical gardens to a private gym and pickleball court, the couple have been making substantial changes while their larger residential project takes shape.Bezos' property purchases on Indian Creek Island have unfolded over several years. Reportedly, in 2023, he acquired two neighbouring mansions for $68 million and $79 million, respectively. The properties form part of a larger plan to create a substantial private estate for himself and his wife.Before that project could become their permanent home, however, the couple needed somewhere to live. In 2024, Bezos purchased another property on the island for $87 million.The Mediterranean-style mansion, set on approximately 1.84 acres, became their primary residence while plans for the neighbouring properties moved forward.The island, commonly known as Billionaire Bunker, is one of South Florida's most exclusive residential addresses. Its appeal lies partly in its waterfront setting and private surroundings, with a small community of exceptionally wealthy residents. NFL legend Tom Brady and Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner are among the high-profile names associated with the neighbourhood.The $87 million property is not the centrepiece of Bezos' long-term plans for Indian Creek. That distinction belongs to the two homes he purchased in 2023. Reports have indicated that the couple intend to demolish both existing structures and replace them with one enormous custom-built mansion. The proposed development would bring the neighbouring plots together as a single residential compound.In the meantime, their third mansion has received considerably more attention than a typical temporary residence might. Rather than simply maintaining the property until the larger estate is ready, Bezos and Sánchez Bezos have undertaken changes affecting both the house and its surrounding grounds.The outdoor transformation has been one of the most visible parts of the renovation. Professional arborists have been brought in to introduce a variety of exotic trees across the front and rear gardens. Among the reported additions are Japanese yews and Brazilian Beauty Leafs. Their placement creates a denser landscape around the property, providing additional screening from neighbouring homes and helping establish a more secluded setting.The landscaping goes beyond planting trees around the boundaries. Several statues have also been installed across the grounds, while paved pathways wind through the rear garden. These routes divide the outdoor space into smaller landscaped areas, giving the large property a series of more enclosed garden settings.For a waterfront mansion occupying 1.84 acres, the changes represent a substantial reworking of the available outdoor space. The result is a property where landscaping, privacy and recreational facilities have become major parts of the renovation.The couple's improvements also include facilities designed for spending time outdoors. Planning applications reviewed by the Realtor indicate that a private pickleball court has been incorporated into the property. The sport has become a popular recreational activity, particularly among affluent homeowners who have sufficient space to install their own courts. At the Bezos residence, it adds another private sporting facility to the grounds.The swimming pool area has also undergone changes. The paved surface around the pool has been extended, creating room for an outdoor dining arrangement beneath a floral canopy.Some of the more expensive alterations have taken place away from the gardens. The property's existing garage has been converted into a private fitness facility, changing the way the building's space is used. The work involved removing the original garage door and installing new industrial-strength doors. According to the Realtor, planning details, the replacement doors alone cost upwards of $100,000.The interior of the mansion has also been subject to aesthetic improvements, alongside structural work involving the heating, ventilation and air-conditioning system, plumbing and electrical installations. The planning applications were submitted through a limited liability company associated with Bezos' purchase of the mansion. The company is managed by attorney John C. Sumberg.The Indian Creek purchases followed Bezos' decision to relocate his primary residence from Washington state to Florida in 2023. At the time, he and Sánchez Bezos indicated that the move would bring him closer to members of his family. Florida also offered a significant financial consideration. A February 2024 report by CNBC estimated that Bezos could avoid at least $610 million in taxes that he might otherwise have owed had he continued living full-time in Washington state.His residential connections to Florida had already extended beyond Indian Creek. In 2022, Bezos purchased two adjacent mansions in Coral Gables for $78 million, creating a home for his parents, Mike and Jackie Bezos. His mother, Jackie, died in August 2025 following a long battle with Lewy Body Dementia. Bezos shared a personal tribute on social media, recalling how she had raised him after becoming a mother at 17 and describing the time he was able to spend with her.The Amazon founder's real estate holdings extend well beyond South Florida. He has retained several properties in Washington state, including a substantial residential estate in Hunts Point, near Seattle. Bezos and his former wife, MacKenzie Scott, initially purchased two homes on a five-acre site in Hunts Point for $10 million, four years after Amazon was founded. The estate was subsequently renovated, with reports placing the cost of the work at approximately $28 million in 2010.The property includes 310 feet of private shoreline and a private boathouse. Bezos later acquired an adjacent 24,000-square-foot mansion, further expanding the estate. His portfolio also includes a Washington, DC, residence purchased for $23 million in 2017, alongside several apartments in a Manhattan building. The New York holdings include a three-storey penthouse and two additional apartments, with building permits filed in 2019 to combine the units.In California, Bezos owns a Beverly Hills mansion purchased from music executive David Geffen for $165 million in 2020. The property has also attracted attention beyond its ownership, serving as the location for Kris Jenner's 70th birthday celebration in 2025. His real estate interests have not remained entirely unchanged. In April 2026, Bezos sold a Seattle-area property for a reported $63 million, having purchased it for $37.5 million in 2019.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos have bought three mansions on Billionaire Bunker in South Florida. The Amazon founder paid $87 million for a third mansion on the island in 2024, adding to two neighbouring properties he had already acquired the previous year. What was expected to serve as temporary accommodation has since become the subject of extensive renovation.

Article Title: As European Union is suing IBM, Atos and Leonardo over missed deadlines, glitches and 'Moscow link'; companies ‘remind’ upset Europe: Don't ignore …
Article Text:
Project derailed by hardware and software glitches

IBM and Atos tell EU: You cannot forget Covid-19

What is fear over 'Moscow Files'

The European Union’s border technology agency has sued IBM, France’s biggest IT company Atos and Italy’s Leonardo over repeated delays in developing its Entry/Exit System (EES). According to a report in the Financial Times, citing internal communications, EU-Lisa, which oversees the system, filed the lawsuit in Estonia in December 2025 after the consortium missed delivery deadlines and challenged warnings and financial penalties, according to the report.The biometric border system was originally due to launch in 2022 but reached full rollout only this year. Its introduction has been marked by technical problems and hours-long airport queues across Europe during the summer.The EES requires travellers from outside the bloc to register fingerprints and photographs when first entering the Schengen area. It is designed to help authorities identify visa overstayers and people wanted by law enforcement. The passport-free travel area covers 29 European countries, most of them European Union ((EU) members.Software and hardware failures have disrupted its introduction, including fingerprint scanners malfunctioning when covered in sweat.Some EU countries are still acquiring scanners, the FT reported. EU-Lisa disclosed the lawsuit in annual accounts published in July, saying that it had pursued contractual and legal remedies following delivery delays to protect its financial interests.Estonia’s Harju county court confirmed that the civil case had been filed. No hearings had taken place or been scheduled, according to the newspaper. EU-Lisa declined to discuss the proceedings but said the case had “no impact on the functioning” of the EES, which it described as fully operational across Europe. The European Commission also said the dispute concerned development delays rather than the system’s operation.Atos and Leonardo declined to comment on the legal proceedings, while IBM did not respond to a request for comment, the FT reported.Correspondence reviewed by the FT shows that disagreements over delivery schedules and penalties stretch back several years. In October 2021, Atos Belgium and IBM Belgium challenged both the basis and calculation of a fine, arguing that external factors, including the Covid-19 pandemic, had caused delays.The three companies subsequently objected to revised deadlines in February 2022, arguing that the timetable was unrealistic and criticising EU-Lisa’s governance of the project. “​​Ignoring reality is not prudent and will not help to achieve the plan,” the consortium reportedly wrote.A month later, an IBM representative agreed that EU-Lisa could withhold some payments pending resolution of the damages dispute. The agency’s 2022 accounts acknowledged difficulties with the consortium and said it was assessing additional costs arising from delays, which had also affected other IT projects. The contract’s total value had already increased from €142 million to €212 million in 2021.Further delays raised hardware and software maintenance expenses. In 2023, EU-Lisa nearly doubled its annual EES budget to €40 million by moving money from other projects, according to accounts cited by the FT.The original contract expired in 2025, and a new consortium took over implementation. IBM, Atos and Leonardo nevertheless remained responsible until August, EU-Lisa said.The project has also faced questions about cybersecurity. It was previously reported that Atos had used its Moscow office to procure software for the border system. EU-Lisa said it had identified no security breaches. According to an internal report reviewed by the newspaper, the EU’s anti-fraud office, Olaf, found sufficient grounds for further investigation and said Russian involvement, if established, would breach the contract.
Article Summary: EU-Lisa sues IBM, Atos and Leonardo over repeated delays in developing its Entry/Exit System. System was originally due to launch in 2022 but reached full rollout only this year. Its introduction has been marked by technical problems and hours-long airport queues.

Article Title: Australian airline Qantas to axe 850 jobs at HQ, shift work to India
Article Text:
Qantas CEO said "sorry for the uncertainty"

What happens to affected Qantas employees?

India is set to handle a major share of outsourced corporate operations of Australian airline Qantas, which plans to transfer around 850 head-office jobs to technology services company Accenture under a multi-year agreement.Most of the services covered by the arrangement will be delivered by Accenture's teams in India, reported various Australian media outlets including Austrlia Broadcasting Company.The transition will cover several business functions, including finance, procurement, human resources and marketing. The first phase is expected to be implemented by mid-2027, with some services continuing to be handled in Australia.The arrangement is part of Qantas' efforts to overhaul its technology infrastructure and simplify its operations as artificial intelligence increasingly reshapes the travel industry. The airline is looking to modernise systems that have become difficult to integrate and manage.Qantas CEO Vanessa Hudson told employees that the company operates more than 1,000 legacy applications that were not designed to work together.“Modernising these systems and connecting the data across them is the critical next step,” she said, adding that the changes would help accelerate innovation and the airline's use of AI.Hudson also acknowledged the uncertainty the announcement could create among employees.“I know this is hard news for some, and I’m sorry for the uncertainty it brings,” she said.Explaining the broader objective, she added, “They are about modernising the technology behind our business and becoming more efficient, so we can keep investing in our customers, our people and our future.”The decision has drawn criticism from the Australian Services Union (ASU), which has questioned the implications of shifting work from Qantas' Australian headquarters to overseas teams.ASU NSW Secretary Angus McFarland said the union believed most of the affected positions were based at the airline's headquarters in Mascot, Sydney.“This should be chilling to not only those workers, but all Australians, because no Australian benefits from this. This is jobs offshore, and this is skills offshore at our national airline,” McFarland said, as quoted by ANI.The union has also alleged that the latest announcement contradicts assurances given to employees earlier this year.ASU Assistant National Secretary Scott Cowen said workers had been told in August that Qantas had no plans to offshore Australian jobs. “Earlier this year, Qantas told us directly there was no plan to offshore any jobs. Today, they’ve come out and told hundreds of staff members that their work will now be delivered mostly from people overseas,” Cowen said.The union is seeking details on how many positions will be affected, which roles will remain in Australia and what retraining assistance will be offered. It has also called for redundancy packages that take employees' years of service into account.Hudson said the individual outcomes for employees had not yet been determined and that the airline would consult workers and their union over the coming months.Qantas has said it intends to retain as many employees as possible within the group by offering opportunities for redeployment, retraining and reskilling.The company is expected to work through these arrangements as the outsourcing transition progresses.
Article Summary: Qantas plans to transfer 850 head-office jobs to Accenture under a multi-year agreement. Most of the services covered by the arrangement will be delivered by Accenture's teams in India. The first phase is expected to be implemented by mid-2027.

Article Title: Books procurement scam: Madras HC directs DVAC to register FIR, freeze bank accounts of fraudulent publishers
Article Text:

MADURAI: Madras high court on Tuesday directed the DVAC to register FIR on the books procurement scam and to freeze the bank accounts of fraudulent publishers.A division bench of Justice G R Swaminathan and Justice M D Sumathi also directed the director of public libraries to submit the list of officials who were responsible for such fraudulent procurement of books.The court passed the order while hearing a contempt petition filed by V Ramasubbu, an advocate from Tirunelveli district, complaining about the non-compliance of an earlier order passed by the court in 2024.In 2019, a public interest litigation filed by S Krishnan of Kanyakumari district seeking a direction to the authorities to take immediate action with regard to illegal purchase of books for public libraries, maintain standard in public libraries and maintain transparent procedures in procuring books for public libraries by uploading the details on their official website.While disposing of the petition in 2024, the court directed the directorate of public libraries to maintain a dedicated website to ensure transparency in the process of purchasing books for public libraries in the state. The court also directed the state government to issue a circular calling upon the heads of educational institutions to make library visits part of the school curriculum. The court also directed the state to constitute a committee to inquire into the allegations made by the petitioner.

Article Title: BRS Seeks High-Level Probe Into Group-I Recruitment Process
Article Text: Hyderabad: The BRS has urged the Telangana State Public Service Commission (TGPSC) to order an independent high-level inquiry into the Group-I recruitment process, citing reports that a significant number of recently selected candidates failed foundational training examinations at the Telangana State Police Academy (TGPA).BRS MLC Dasoju Sravan and other leaders Gellu Srinivas Yadav met TGPSCL chairman Burra Venkatesham on Tuesday and submitted a representation. The leaders said that nearly 35 percent of trainee Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSPs) selected through the Group-I recruitment process reportedly failed academy examinations despite undergoing training for several months. The BRS said that such a high failure rate raises serious questions about the integrity of the recruitment and evaluation process.The BRS leaders said that the issue warrants a forensic examination of the Group-I Mains examination and selection procedures. “Three possibilities need to be examined: shortcomings in academy training, deficiencies in the recruitment and evaluation process, or potential manipulation of marks and rankings. The Commission cannot dismiss other possibilities without conducting an independent verification,” Dasoju Sravan said.Referring to earlier litigation over the Group-I examination, Sravan said that while the Telangana High Court and later the Supreme Court declined to interfere with the recruitment process, those decisions were based on the material available at that time. The party leader said that the alleged poor performance of selected candidates in training constitutes new evidence that merits fresh scrutiny by the Commission.Sravan asked the commission to constitute an independent inquiry panel headed by a sitting High Court judge, collection and examination of academy performance records, preservation of examination-related evidence, and publication of inquiry findings.ends/
Article Summary: The BRS has urged the Telangana State Public Service Commission to order an independent high-level inquiry into the Group-I recruitment process. BRS MLC Dasoju Sravan and other leaders met TGPSCL chairman Burra Venkatesham on Tuesday and submitted a representation.

Article Title: 373 or 1,747? What was Delhi's actual AQI on Diwali and why did readings differ
Article Text:
(PTI Photo) The left image shows the North Block on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, and the right image shows the same location on Monday, Nov. 9.

A thick layer of smog engulfs an area near the Yamuna river in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)

How is AQI calculated?

Particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10)

Ground-level ozone (O₃)

Carbon monoxide (CO)

Sulphur dioxide (SO₂)

Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)

breakpoints

How AQI is calculated

India calculates using 24-hr averages

Jahangirpuri's PM2.5 hits 4,985, DPCC later revises reading

PM 2.5 over 330 times WHO limit

Readings kept disappearing and changing

PM10 levels also soar across Delhi

Image Credit: PTI

Why do different apps show different AQI readings?

What does CPCB say?

What CPCB said





NEW DELHI: Social media was flooded with screenshots of air quality apps showing Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI) touching 1,500 to 1,800 on Diwali night, even as the official figures shared by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) remained below 400.The discrepancy has raised questions about how different platforms calculate air pollution levels and why their readings vary so widely.While India's National Air Quality Index (NAQI), used by CPCB, is capped at 500, several international platforms follow methodologies based on the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which does not impose the same upper limit.But beyond the difference in AQI scores, pollution monitoring data from Delhi showed just how severe the spike in particulate matter was after firecrackers were set off on Diwali night.TOI explains how different AQI methodologies work, why readings vary and what pollution monitoring stations recorded across the capital.The Air Quality Index measures the concentration of major air pollutants, including:For each pollutant, predetermined concentration limits, known as, are used to convert measured pollution levels into an AQI score. The score is then assigned to a category indicating the severity of air pollution.India's AQI has six categories, ranging from Good (0-50) to Severe (401-500). The US system also has six categories, but its uppermost category, Hazardous, has no equivalent 500-point ceiling.This means that while India's system stops displaying increasingly high pollution levels beyond 500, platforms following the US methodology can continue assigning higher numerical scores.The concentration at which a pollutant enters a particular category also varies between the two systems. A lower breakpoint means that the category is reached at a lower pollutant concentration.For instance, the upper concentration limits under the Good category and the concentrations at which the Severe or Hazardous categories begin are not identical across the two methodologies.However, a direct comparison requires accounting for differences in pollutant averaging periods. India generally uses 24-hour averages for several pollutants, while the US system uses different averaging periods, including one-hour and eight-hour averages for certain pollutants.Nitrogen dioxide, for example, is assessed using a 24-hour average in India and a one-hour average in the US. Comparing the numerical thresholds without accounting for these differences can be misleading.Similarly, the US EPA's Good-category ozone breakpoint is based on an eight-hour concentration table, rather than its one-hour table.The hourly PM2.5 concentration at northwest Delhi's Jahangirpuri spiked to 4,985 micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³) at 6 pm and 8 pm on Diwali, before shooting up again at 8 am the next day, making it the most polluted location on Sunday and Monday in the city.This was around 83 times the daily national ambient air quality standard of 60 µg/m³ and over 332 times the World Health Organisation's (WHO) daily safe guideline of 15 µg/m³.However, the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) changed the readings on Monday night, showing that Jahangirpuri had hit its peak PM2.5 level at 776 µg/m³ at Diwali midnight.The pattern of extreme pollution around midnight was witnessed in most parts of the city when firecrackers were set off in large numbers.A TOI analysis of DPCC real-time air quality data shows that most monitoring stations witnessed a sharp rise in PM2.5 levels around midnight. Thereafter, pollution levels remained high till at least 6 am on Monday.At Mundka, hourly PM2.5 levels jumped from 245 µg/m³ at 7 pm on Diwali to 3,744 µg/m³ at 2 am on Monday. A similar trend was witnessed across the city.JNU saw a peak hourly PM2.5 concentration of 3,023 µg/m³ at 4 am on Monday, compared with 118 µg/m³ at 7 pm on Sunday. The peak reading at NSUT (west campus) was 3,008 µg/m³, while Mandir Marg recorded 2,908 µg/m³.Other stations that recorded hazardous hourly PM2.5 levels included Nehru Nagar in Lajpat Nagar (2,808 µg/m³), Wazirpur (2,721), Talkatora Garden (2,599), CWG Sports Complex in Akshardham (2,471), Patparganj (2,597) and Ashok Vihar (2,589).Several locations in Delhi also recorded high hourly PM10 concentrations.At Punjabi Bagh, PM10 reached 4,697 µg/m³, nearly 47 times the daily national ambient air quality standard of 100 µg/m³. It was more than 104 times WHO's daily safe guideline of 45 µg/m³.Hourly PM10 concentrations also surged to 3,490 µg/m³ at Anand Vihar, 3,929 at Patparganj, 2,881 at RK Puram, 2,879 at Nehru Nagar and 2,671 at Wazirpur.Sunil Dahiya, founder of think tank Envirocatalyst, said, “Through Diwali night, people across Delhi inhaled PM2.5 averaging 450 to 550 µg/m³. That is eight to nine times the national 24-hour standard and 30 to 37 times WHO's guideline. Even a few hours at these levels can trigger asthma attacks, worsen lung diseases and raise the risk of heart attacks and strokes.”Dahiya said children, the elderly, pregnant women, outdoor workers and people with heart or lung conditions were hit hardest in such situations.“Fine particles reach deep into their lungs and bloodstream, and the coarser PM10 inflames airways and eyes. One night was added to a season in which Delhi's air was already more than twice the safe limit before a single cracker was burst,” he said.Differences in methodology are not the only reason behind the mismatch. The sources from which platforms obtain pollution data also play a role.CPCB collects raw pollution readings from Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS), which form part of the official monitoring network.Several private air-quality platforms, meanwhile, rely on a combination of government monitoring stations and privately operated sensors. Some also use readings from non-regulatory-grade instruments, including low-cost sensors.The calibration, accuracy and data quality of these instruments can vary, potentially contributing to differences in the readings displayed by different platforms.The averaging period used to calculate AQI can also affect the final number. An hourly reading may capture a sudden pollution spike, while a 24-hour average smoothens such fluctuations.CPCB has clarified that AQI methodologies adopted by agencies other than it may use breakpoint concentrations different from those prescribed under India's National Air Quality Index.It has maintained that the NAQI published by CPCB is India's official AQI for public dissemination and that other AQI figures are not recognised for regulatory or reporting purposes.The board has also pointed out that several global air-quality platforms and private organisations obtain information from both government and non-government sources, including non-regulatory-grade monitoring instruments.Such low-cost sensors may have calibration and data-quality limitations, CPCB said.As a result, readings from different platforms should not be treated as directly interchangeable. A figure exceeding 1,000 on an international app does not necessarily mean CPCB's official AQI has crossed the same numerical threshold. The two may be measuring and presenting air pollution using different scales, averaging periods and data sources.
